avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction reduces tiagabine levels and efficacy; may precipitate seizures
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; do not use concurrently with tiagabine

avoid_supplements.name: Valerian Root
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive CNS depression and sedation; may increase seizure risk with abrupt discontinuation
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; discuss with healthcare provider before use

caution_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild anticonvulsant properties; potential additive effects on seizure threshold
caution_supplements.action: Monitor seizure control if used; report any changes in seizure frequency

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplementation
caution_supplements.mechanism: May enhance GABAergic activity; theoretical additive CNS effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased sedation; maintain consistent dosing if using

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase tiagabine absorption and peak concentrations; potential for increased side effects
caution_foods.action: Take tiagabine consistently with or without food; avoid large fatty meals immediately before dosing

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive CNS depression; increased risk of sedation, dizziness, and impaired cognition
caution_foods.action: Limit or avoid alcohol consumption; educate patient on increased fall and seizure risk

monitoring_notes: Monitor for seizure control, sedation, and cognitive effects. Tiagabine has a narrow therapeutic index and is susceptible to CYP3A4 interactions; advise patients to maintain consistent dosing timing and report any changes in seizure frequency or CNS symptoms.
